label: Multi-Block Structures
title: Multi-block structures
lead: Planned documentation for structures made from multiple world blocks.
bodyHtml:
What this API is for

StructureRegistry is for authored multi-block structures exported from the CU Structure Editor / More Structures webapp as v2 JSON. This won't work to replace BuildingEntityRegistry, designed for structures instead.

Structure editor

Create the structure layout in the sister webtool CU-Custom-Structures editor, export the compact v2 JSON, then register that exported payload through StructureRegistry.

Whilst the structure editor awaits its own update, you may choose to edit the .json file by hand to include custom tiles/buildingentites/etc, which will work.

Register structure JSON

Author the structure in the webapp, export the compact v2 JSON, and register that exact payload. You can load the text from an embedded resource or a loose file path.

string campJson = AssetLoader.LoadEmbeddedText("Structures.camp_heater_room.json");
StructureRegistry.RegisterFromJson("campheaterroom", campJson);

StructureRegistry.RegisterFromEmbeddedJson(
    "fieldlab",
    "Structures.field_lab.json");

StructureRegistry.RegisterFromFile(
    "crashsite",
    Path.Combine(Paths.PluginPath, "MyMod", "Structures", "crashsite.json"));

The structure ID is the stable runtime key. The exported JSON keeps ownership of the actual block/object/item layout and the default five-depth spawnCounts values.

Spawn counts and overrides

The importer reuses the same five-depth spawnCounts array the structure editor already exports. If your mod wants to tweak density after import, override the counts in code without rewriting the JSON.

StructureRegistry.RegisterFromEmbeddedJson(
    "fieldlab",
    "Structures.field_lab.json");

StructureRegistry.TrySetSpawnCounts("fieldlab", 0, 1, 2, 2, 3);

During world generation, CUCoreLib reads the current biome depth, picks the matching count, and places the already-compiled structure payload for each spawn.
